passage.title: SECOND-HAND TREASURES
passage.subtitle: Oliver's vintage clothes shop
paragraphs: Near the main train station in Bath, Oliver runs a small shop called Second-Hand Treasures. He buys clean, good-quality vintage clothes from local people and sells them at low prices to students and tourists.

Inside the shop, wooden shelves are full of denim jackets, colourful scarves, leather bags and old vinyl records. There is also a quiet corner with a large mirror and a blue curtain where customers can try on coats and dresses.

Oliver checks every item carefully before putting it on a hanger. If a jacket is missing a button or has a small hole, he repairs it himself on a sewing machine at the back of the shop. He says good clothes should last for many years instead of going into the rubbish.
Every Friday afternoon, university students visit the shop to look for unusual outfits for weekend parties. Oliver enjoys helping them find something special that nobody else is wearing.
